summary: Comprehensive backend API + light frontend smoke test for Medalyze HRMS. Backend: 37/38 pytest tests passed (97%). One real bug found: login rate-limit lockout is inverted and never triggers 429. Frontend loads, login works, dashboard renders with correct KPIs, sidebar navigation testids present.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout does NOT trigger. In routers/auth.py line ~70, the ternary sets locked_until to a FUTURE time only when cnt < MAX_ATTEMPTS, and to current-time when cnt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS. This is inverted, so after 5+ wrong passwords the API keeps returning 401 instead of 429. Fix: swap branches -> `_lock_iso() if cnt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS else iso(now_utc()...)`. Verified via test_rate_limiting_lockout (5 wrong attempts -> got 401, expected 429).

action_items: Fix inverted rate-limit lockout condition in /app/backend/routers/auth.py (login handler) — currently locked_until is set to now on the 5th failure instead of now+15min, so 429 never returns.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/auth.py login: locked_until ternary is inverted (see action item). Also the initial check compares `locked_until > now_utc()`, but on the 5th attempt locked_until is set to current time (immediately expired) — reinforcing the bug.

routers/leave.py list_requests: control-flow for `scope`/role filtering is convoluted (an inner `if is_admin(user) and scope != 'team': pass` inside a manager branch). Consider refactor for clarity; behavior currently correct in tested cases.
routers/attendance.py enrich_attendance leaks scheduled fields via clean() — acceptable, but audit fields aren't stripped from `shift_snapshot` on GET.
routers/reports.py has no date range validation; large orgs could hit the 5000 limit silently. Add pagination/warning.
routers/employees.py list_employees: raises 403 AFTER building query — minor; move check to top (already effectively first per code path, fine).
server.py CORS uses `os.environ.get('CORS_ORIGINS', '*').split(',')` with `allow_credentials=True` — if CORS_ORIGINS is unset, browsers will reject `*` with credentials. Ensure env is set in prod.

routers/clients.py list_portals returns portals for any user assigned to the client, including employees — verify by design (employees can view masked list but not reveal since reveal requires `client.portal.reveal` permission).

rca of the issue: AuthN rate-limit RCA: In /app/backend/routers/auth.py the failed-login handler upserts a login_attempts record with `locked_until = iso(now_utc()) if cnt < MAX_ATTEMPTS else _lock_iso()`. The ternary is inverted — when cnt is below the threshold the code writes a FUTURE-in-name-only stamp equal to `now_utc()`, and only when cnt reaches MAX it should lock (`_lock_iso()` = now+15min) but the branches are swapped. Result: on the 5th failure, `locked_until` is set to the current instant which is immediately in the past, so the guard `locked_until > now_utc()` is false and login continues to return 401 forever. Reproduction: POST /api/auth/login 6 times with a bad password for the same email — expected 429 on the 6th call, actual 401. Mitigation: swap the branches: `"locked_until": _lock_iso() if cnt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS else iso(now_utc().replace(microsecond=0))`. Optionally also index login_attempts by identifier and purge on TTL.
